close_reason:
Closing as opinion / no engineering basis to change.

Current shape correctly reflects inner-loop semantics:
- create/update use `args.get()` because the inner loops iterate `.keys()` only (no Value ownership needed)
- destroy uses `args.remove()` because the inner code consumes the Array

The bead's premise — that the other three /set handlers (calendar.rs, event.rs, participant_identity.rs) consistently use .remove() — is true for those specific handlers, but their inner loops DO consume values (`for (create_id, obj_val) in create_map`), unlike event_notification.rs whose inner loops only need keys.

Workspace canonical mail-server is itself inconsistent across the same boundary:
- email.rs:1168/1257/1325 — get/remove/get
- mailbox.rs:544/722/961 — get/remove/get
- identity.rs:224/333/414 — remove/remove/remove
- vacation.rs:189/199/360 — get/remove/get
- submission.rs:471/510/565 — get/remove/get

So there's no canonical convergence target — mail-server uses `.get()` for create/update when the inner code doesn't need ownership, matching event_notification.rs's current shape.

The inline comments at event_notification.rs:143/153/163 (`// create — forbidden`, `// update — forbidden`, `// destroy — the only permitted operation`) already make the read-only-vs-consuming distinction implicit. Adding an explicit `// .get() because we only iterate keys` comment would be belt-and-suspenders.

Stopping here per the workspace bikeshedding-signal rule.
description:
event_notification.rs:92-109 — handle_calendar_event_notification_set reads:

  if let Some(create_map) = args.get('create').and_then(|v| v.as_object()) { ... }
  if let Some(update_map) = args.get('update').and_then(|v| v.as_object()) { ... }

…and at line 112 reads:

  if let Some(Value::Array(destroy_arr)) = args.remove('destroy') { ... }

The reason the destroy path uses .remove() is to take ownership of the Vec<Value>. The reason create/update use .get() is that the handler returns 'forbidden' without consuming the inner map. That works but it is a small inconsistency that took me a re-read to confirm wasn't a bug.

The other three /set handlers (calendar.rs, event.rs, participant_identity.rs) consistently use .remove() for all three maps because they consume each entry.

Two cleanups (pick one):

(a) Switch the create/update paths to args.remove(...) for shape consistency with siblings. The remove discards the Value, so it costs nothing.

(b) Add a one-line comment explaining the intentional asymmetry, e.g. '// read-only access — destroy needs ownership of the array'.

P4 readability — no behavior change. The case for (a) is the cookie-cutter rule (other handlers use .remove()), and the case for (b) is preserving the slightly cheaper code path.
title: CalendarEventNotification/set inconsistently reads create/update via .get() but destroy via .remove()
